Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Vantorre CX-10: repeated E34 lockouts and disputed site-water diagnosis

We bought the refurbished 2021 Vantorre CX-10 (serial VT21-30877) for $14,800 including GST. It was delivered and commissioned on 14 September. The listing stated that the steam generator had been descaled and pressure tested and the core probe calibrated, with six months’ parts-and-labour warranty. Warranty registration runs to 14 March 2027.

On 22 September, service report SR-1190 recorded nine E34 steam-generator low-water-level events since 14 September. The level sensor was replaced, inlet pressure measured 320 kPa and three steam cycles tested satisfactorily. That visit was covered by warranty at no charge.

By 3 October, E34 had returned four times that week. The core probe was also reading low: during two checks on a lamb shoulder, the oven displayed 63°C while our Thermapen read 70°C. On 6 October, report SR-1236 recorded heavy steam-generator scaling. The generator was descaled and flushed, and the probe recalibrated to within one degree. Kelsall recommended a softener, attributing the scale to our supply.

Our water supplier subsequently advised that average Fitzroy hardness is approximately 15 mg/L as CaCO3, which it classifies as soft. The oven had been on our water for only 22 days when the heavy scale was found, despite being advertised as descaled. Those figures do not support dismissing the problem simply as a hard-water site. We cannot establish where the scale originated, but that question remains unanswered.

At 6.10pm on Saturday 24 October, E34 locked us out during dinner with 60 covers booked. We finished the lamb on the stove and in the deck oven, removed the pork belly from the menu and absorbed that cost.

Kelsall’s 28 October email states that Dion again found E34 and further scale on 27 October. Six weeks after delivery, and within the registered warranty period, we were told that attendance would be invoiced at $280 plus GST ($308 including GST) as a site-water issue.

Other kitchens spending close to $15,000 on a refurbished combi should be able to consider this full fault history, the measured water information and the possibility of a callout charge during the advertised warranty period.
